newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fiat trims Argentine investment, raises Brazilian.
newsitem.headline: Fiat trims Argentine investment, raises Brazilian.

text.p: Fiat's Argentine truck unit IVECO downgraded a planned investment in Argentina in favor of Brazil due to local union unrest and car incentives offered by Brazil, a Fiat spokesman said Monday.
"IVECO had planned to invest $120 million to upgrade its plant in Cordoba province to produce the light truck Daily, and the Ducato van," the spokesman, who asked no to be identified, told Reuters.
He added the company had also planned a minor investment to build a heavy truck plant in Brazil.

"Now, with the decision taken in the last few days, the terms are inverted," he said. "The company will make heavy trucks in Argentina with a lesser investment and invest more in the new Brazilian plant to make light vehicles."
The investment in Argentina will fall to less than half of the $120 million originally slated, he said.
"The decision is taken on the base of union conflicts in Cordoba and the incentives offered by the Brazilian government for the car sector."

Unions in Cordoba are at odds over who has the right to represent Fiat workers. The company laid off 40 employees who in January occupied the plant during a week in protest against the layoff of another worker.
The provincial government ordered mandatory negotiations between workers and the carmaker but the Fiat spokesman said it will not rehire any of them.
"We are just discussing on an individual basis economic terms for the layoffs and that is just for the cases where compensation applies," the spokesman said.
Argentina and Brazil, together with Paraguay and Uruguay, are members of the customs unions Mercosur.
Argentina has filed a protest to the Brazilian government alleging unfair incentives for the car industry.
In December Fiat opened a $600 million plant in Cordoba as part of its strategy to make Mercosur a key market for its vehicles.

In Cordoba it will make different versions of the Siena compact car, which will hit the road in April. The Siena is part of Fiat's "Project 178," a plan that gave birth to the Palio, the second best-selling car in Brazil, where it was launched last year.
